finding.claim: The /checkout endpoint computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty. An attacker can set price to 0 or a tiny value to buy items for free. They can also send a negative price or qty to make the total negative, which may produce a refund or credit. The server never looks up the catalog price, and it does not validate that qty is a positive integer. The legacy /checkout route sits next to the safer /checkout-v2, which does look up prices.
finding.sink: req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) at cart.js:6, which charges the attacker-computed amount

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, using values taken straight from the request body
total is passed to payments.charge with no server-side price check, no minimum of 0, and no type check
the response returns the attacker-chosen total as charged

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization middleware appears in this file, and req.user is assumed to be set upstream. There is no input validation on price or qty, no catalog price lookup, no check that total > 0, and no integer or finite-number check. The only controls I could not see are middleware outside this file.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js; no auth/validation middleware on the router, and cart.js is the only file in the directory. The /checkout-v2 route (cart.js:14) shows the intended controls (catalog price lookup, qty clamp), which /checkout lacks.
verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty, and cart.js:6 passes that total to payments.charge with no catalog lookup or bounds check, so an authenticated user can set price to 0 or a negative value, while /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) does look up prices.

verdict_facts.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty, cart.js:6 charges that total with no catalog lookup or range check (unlike /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14), and cart.js:7 returns it, so any authenticated user can set price to 0 or negative.
